question: Which international organization publishes air quality guidelines that many nations use as a reference?

options.text: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

solution:
The correct answer is __**World Health Organization (WHO)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** is the primary international organization responsible for publishing **Air Quality Guidelines (AQGs)**, which serve as a global reference for air quality standards.
 
• These guidelines are essential for countries to develop their own air quality standards to protect public health from the adverse effects of air pollution.
 
• WHO published its latest **Global Air Quality Guidelines** in **September 2021**, updating previous guidelines that were last revised in 2005, based on the latest scientific evidence.
 
• The guidelines target key air pollutants such as **particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10), ozone (O3), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), sulfur dioxide (SO2), and carbon monoxide (CO)**.
 
• WHO’s guidelines are widely used by nations to design policies and strategies to improve air quality and mitigate the health impacts of air pollution.
 
• They aim to reduce the burden of diseases caused by air pollution, which includes illnesses like **respiratory infections, heart diseases, and lung cancer**.
